## Valuation & Funding

Midjourney has not raised external funding and remains completely self-funded since its founding in 2021. The company operates with approximately 40-45 employees and has built its $200M+ ARR business entirely through organic growth and reinvested profits.

Founder David Holz has maintained the company's independence by rejecting venture capital, allowing Midjourney to operate without external investor pressure or dilution. This approach has enabled the company to focus on product development and user experience rather than growth metrics typically demanded by venture investors.

results.title: How Many People Work At Midjourney 2026: Lean Team • SQ Magazine
results.author: Barry Elad
highlights:
Midjourney employs roughly 40 to 165 people across its distributed team as of mid-2025, with Sacra reporting figures from 40 to 45 in its company profile and 163 in May 2025, while pulling in an estimated $500 million in annual revenue. Founder David Holz stated in August 2022 that the company was already profitable. We’re like about 10 people. We’re self-funded. We have no investors. The headcount has grown since, but staying small is the defining business choice that separates Midjourney from every venture-funded peer in generative AI.

The data below covers the headcount timeline from 11 employees in 2022 to roughly 163 in 2025, revenue per employee that crossed $5 million at peak, the bootstrap funding history, product release cadence, Discord community size, and how the team compares with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia.

...

- Midjourney started with about 10 people in August 2022, when founder David Holz told The Register the firm was already profitable.
- The team scaled to roughly 40 employees by the end of 2023, the year Midjourney crossed $200 million in annual recurring revenue.
- LinkedIn-derived counts cited by Sacra and Contrary Research place the headcount at 131 in September 2024 and 163 by May 2025.
- Revenue per employee reached an estimated $5 million at the 2023 ARR mark, settling near $3.07 million at the 2025 figure of $500 million across 163 staff.
- Midjourney has raised $0 in external funding since its August 2021 founding, an outlier among generative AI firms that have collectively raised tens of billions.
- The company supports a Discord community of roughly 21 million members with under 200 employees, a community-to-staff ratio above 100,000 to 1.

...

- Midjourney’s confirmed 2022 staffing figure was about 10 people, per founder David Holz’s interview with The Register in August 2022.
- The team grew to roughly 40 employees by 2023, the year revenue reached $200 million ARR, per Contrary Research.
- LinkedIn-traceable counts cited by industry analysts placed the headcount at 131 in September 2024, a roughly 1,090% increase from the 2022 base.
- Sacra and Contrary Research separately cite 163 employees for May 2025, the period when revenue crossed roughly $500 million ARR.
- Sacra’s standalone profile lists a tighter range of 40 to 45 employees, indicating that headcount estimates vary significantly across LinkedIn snapshots and analyst reports.
- The company has been headquartered in San Francisco since its founding in August 2021, operating a largely distributed workforce of fewer than 200 staff, per Wikipedia.

## Midjourney Founding Story And Team Structure

- Midjourney was founded by David Holz in August 2021, per Sacra. Holz previously co-founded Leap Motion in 2011, which Ultrahaptics acquired in May 2019 for approximately $30 million.
- The company describes itself as a “self-funded research lab” rather than a traditional startup, a phrase Holz used directly in the August 2022 Register interview.
- The original team prioritized engineers over operators, with no dedicated sales or business development staff in the early years.
- Holz framed the philosophy bluntly in the same interview: “We’re not like a startup that raises a lot of money and then isn’t sure what their product is and loses money for a long time. We’re like a self-funded research lab.”
- Per Sacra, the team operates remotely with a small core in San Francisco, where the company is registered.
- Decision-making sits with engineering and research staff rather than a layered management hierarchy, a pattern Holz attributed to keeping the team under 50 for as long as practical.

...

- Midjourney’s registered headquarters sits in San Francisco, California, per Wikipedia.
- The company operates without a large central office, with most of the team working remotely, per Sacra reporting.
- No public job board lists multiple regional offices, unlike OpenAI (San Francisco, London, Tokyo) or Anthropic (San Francisco, London, Dublin).
- The remote-first model keeps overhead low and matches the bootstrap discipline that defines the company’s funding philosophy.
- Holz himself splits time between research work and product direction, with no chief operating officer or chief financial officer publicly listed.
- Engineering, research, and limited support roles make up the bulk of the staffing footprint.

The compact office presence is part of why staffing estimates vary so widely. Without a published org chart or filings, third-party counts depend on the LinkedIn signal, which under-represents non-LinkedIn users common in research-heavy teams. The remote-first pattern is increasingly common across AI firms, a trend visible in our AI agent adoption data.

...

How many employees does Midjourney have in 2025?

Midjourney employs roughly 163 people as of May 2025, per figures cited by industry analysts. Some snapshots place the count between 40 and 45 depending on whether contractors and part-time research staff are included. The company has scaled from about 10 employees in 2022 to its 2025 size.

Midjourney was founded in 2022 by David Holz (CEO). Prior to founding Midjourney, Holz described himself as having been a serial entrepreneur since high school, when he ran a design business while still a student. He studied physics and math in college and before going on to pursue a Ph.D. in applied math, while working simultaneously at NASA and the Max Planck Institute from 2009 through 2011.

...

In August 2021, Holz left Leap Motion, seeking a change from large venture-backed companies. Amidst breakthroughs in natural language processing and generative adversarial networks (GANs), Holz recruited a team of ten engineers to start training diffusion models, which resulted in the launch of Midjourney. Midjourney reportedly generated $200 million in revenue in 2023 and is estimated to be operating at $500 million ARR as of May 2025. What makes this particularly notable is that Midjourney has done so without raising outside capital and with a team of just ~40 employees. It is frequently cited as the leanest high-growth AI company in the world, and a standout example of product-market fit in the consumer AI space.
